risks: The access log is durable but unbounded: nothing prunes it. A retention policy (and the regulatory question of how long a privileged-read record must be kept) is a follow-up, not a defect - erring toward keeping the record is the safe direction.

The log records user_id as a value, not a FK, so a query joining to users will silently drop rows for deleted accounts. That is deliberate (the record must outlive the account) but a reader must not assume an inner join is complete.

commits_this_run.subject: feat(governance): store the operator access log so a privileged read survives a restart

decisions_this_run: D-072a: order `recent()` by the surrogate autoincrement id, not by `at`. The port promises newest-first and two reads can share a timestamp; sorting on a shared value is implementation-defined, and an audit trail that can reorder itself is not evidence of sequence.
D-072b: user_id is a plain indexed value, not a FK to users and not cascading. Deleting a user must not erase the record of what that user read.
D-072c: the adapter commits its own session rather than joining the caller's unit of work. The record that the operator SAW the view must land even if the caller's content transaction rolls back.
D-072d: no backfill. The ring was never durable, so there is no earlier table whose rows this could reconstruct.

head_drift_policy: `commit` names the last head whose *product* code was verified by CI, not necessarily the branch tip. NEXUS checkpoint updates are themselves docs-only commits, so the tip advances one commit past `commit` every time this file is written - chasing it is an unbounded loop (run 64 hit this: 7456a89 -> 974d03f -> c49befe, each fix creating a new tip). On reconciliation, compare the product tree, not the SHA: `git diff <commit>..HEAD -- src/ tests/` being empty means `commit` is still an accurate description of what CI verified.
commit_note: A checkpoint commit cannot name itself. 787ed57 is the last substantive commit; every later commit on this branch is a docs-only checkpoint that descends from it, so its CI still compiles and tests the same product code. To find the live head, poll `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/feature/agentic-enterprise-platform` rather than trusting this field. Each such docs commit also cancels the previous head's in-flight CI (branch concurrency), so `conclusion: cancelled` means superseded, never failed.
